summary: Nyunzu territory (Tanganyika) was the epicentre of the 2016-2020 Twa-Luba conflict, with Twa militias ('Elements') and Luba self-defence groups attacking villages along the Nyunzu-Kalemie and Nyunzu-Kabalo axes and around the Kisengo coltan mine. FARDC operations, MONUSCO-backed reconciliation and DDR reduced violence, and no source available to this assessment reports durable armed-group control of any locality in 2025-2026. Nyunzu town is assessed as police-run with FARDC and ANR presence, and Kisengo as a state-held mining town. Villages near the main axes are assessed as thin state presence with possible Twa militia raids. The north-western hinterland toward Bigobo/Mbulula and Kahinda, where Twa militias were most persistent, is assessed as FARDC-held but contested. Live web research was unavailable (search budget exhausted, news and NGO sites blocked), so confidence is low.

sources.title: DR Congo: Escalating violence in Tanganyika

zones.description: Nyunzu town (territory seat; Mangala and Tchangatchanga health areas/neighbourhoods)
zones.evidence: Nyunzu town hosts the territorial administration, PNC commissariat, an FARDC presence and IDP sites from the Twa-Luba conflict. It remained in state hands throughout the 2016-2020 crisis; no report available indicates armed-group control since.

zones.description: Kisengo coltan mining town (Kisengo health area, GRID3 'Hopital')
zones.evidence: Kisengo is a large artisanal coltan mining centre with police (incl. mines police) and army posts; its surroundings saw Twa militia attacks during the Twa-Luba conflict. No 2025-2026 report of armed-group control was available.

zones.description: Villages along the main axes and in central/eastern/northern Nyunzu (Kabeya Mayi, Masamba, Mulongo, Muhuya, Kalima, Kilunga, Kankwaka, Zongwe, Mukundi, Ngoy, Mangala rural)
zones.evidence: These areas were affected by Twa-Luba violence in 2016-2020 but later reports describe sporadic incidents rather than territorial control; thin PNC/ANR presence with FARDC positions on the Nyunzu-Kalemie and Nyunzu-Kabalo axes is assumed.

zones.description: North-western and western hinterland (Lengwe, Butondo/Mulunguy, Sulumba, Kahinda, Kitengetenge, Mbeya, Kanunu, Lwizi, Bigobo/Mbulula HZ and Kashale HA villages)
zones.evidence: The forested hinterland west and north-west of Nyunzu toward Bigobo/Mbulula and Kabalo was where Twa militias held out longest and attacks continued after 2020; the army is assessed as the main permanent force with residual Twa militia activity. No 2025-2026 source could be verified.
